member.name: T:Ethar.GeoPose.Conventions.CompassHeading
member.summary: Conversions between compass bearings and GeoPose Basic-YPR yaw.

remarks.para: A compass bearing is measured clockwise from true North: North 0°, East 90°, South 180°, West 270°. Device compasses, map bearings and most user interfaces use this convention.

GeoPose Basic-YPR yaw (OGC GeoPose 1.0, /req/basic-ypr/angles) is a rotation of the LTP-ENU frame about its Up axis. ENU is right-handed, so positive yaw is counter-clockwise viewed from above, turning East towards North. The standard assigns pitch to the y axis and roll to the x axis, the aircraft convention in which x is the longitudinal (forward) axis, so the un-rotated inner frame faces East (its x axis) and a yaw of 90° faces North.

The two conventions are related by yaw = 90 - bearing, which is its own inverse. The standard does not state the sign convention or the forward axis in words; the reading above follows from its axis assignment and from the right-handed frame, and is the reading these helpers implement.

member.summary: Conversions between the right-handed LTP-ENU frame and a left-handed, Y-up engine frame (Unity's world space), with a heading offset.

remarks.para: The axis mapping is East to +X, Up to +Y and North to +Z. Because the two frames have opposite handedness, this swap alone is not enough for rotations: a rotation by θ about an ENU axis becomes a rotation by -θ about the mapped axis. In quaternion terms an ENU quaternion (x, y, z, w) becomes (-x, -z, -y, w) in the engine frame.

The heading offset is the compass bearing of the engine's +Z axis, in degrees, clockwise from true North. Engines that start their world frame at the device's initial pose have an arbitrary heading offset; a QR code or tracked image with a known GeoPose gives a measured one. True North lies at engine yaw -heading offset. Every ENU displacement and every ENU rotation is therefore turned by -heading offset about the engine's Y axis after the axis mapping, and by +heading offset before mapping back. Use to obtain the offset from a device compass reading.

member.summary: A construct that represents yaw, pitch, and roll angles specified in decimal degrees.
